title: Mock 4 · Theory Meets Rules
blurb: MPT/CAPM basics mixed with PMS regulation, plus a portfolio beta caselet.

questions.q: Under the Companies Act, 2013, an offer to subscribe to securities made to fewer than how many persons is a private placement?
questions.explanation: Section 2.2.1: an offer made to less than 200 persons is called private placement.
hints: Old limit, not as per the workbook.

questions.q: Which cash flow and discount rate pairing correctly gives the value of a firm's EQUITY directly?
options: FCFF discounted at the cost of equity
FCFE discounted at the cost of equity
Dividends discounted at the cost of debt
questions.explanation: Section 3.4: FCFF is discounted by WACC to value the firm; FCFE by cost of equity to value equity.
hints: Cost of debt is not the equity discount rate.

questions.q: A bond has a Macaulay duration of 6 years and pays semi-annual coupons; its YTM is 10% p.a. Its modified duration is about:
questions.explanation: MD = MacD/(1 + YTM/frequency) = 6/1.05 = 5.71 (Section 4.5.2).

questions.q: Open interest in a derivatives market represents:
options: The number of contracts traded during the day
The premium paid on all options
The total number of outstanding contracts that have not been settled
questions.explanation: Section 5.6: open interest is the total number of outstanding derivative contracts not yet settled; it is not trading volume.

questions.q: The Net Asset Value (NAV) of a mutual fund unit is calculated as:
options: Total assets divided by the number of investors
Net assets (market value of assets plus income minus expenses) divided by units outstanding
Market price of units on the stock exchange
questions.explanation: Section 6.9: net assets divided by the number of outstanding units gives NAV.
hints: That is the traded price of close-ended units.

questions.q: Which of the following is a DON'T for portfolio managers?
options: Segregating each client's holdings in separate accounts
Keeping client funds in a separate bank account
Deploying clients' funds in bill discounting or badla financing
Abiding by the code of conduct
questions.explanation: Section 7.6.3 Don'ts: no deployment in bill discounting, badla financing, or lending to corporate/non-corporate bodies.

questions.q: In addition to the Principal Officer and Compliance Officer, a portfolio manager applicant must employ at least one person with:
options: A CFA charter and 10 years' experience
Graduation and at least 2 years' experience in related securities market activities
questions.explanation: Section 7.4 point 5: at least one other employee with graduation and 2 years' experience.
hints: That resembles Principal Officer requirements, not this employee.

questions.q: In a PMS joint holding, dividends, interest and redemption proceeds are paid to:
options: Each holder in proportion to contribution
Any holder nominated at each payout
questions.explanation: Section 8.4.2: investment records are created in the name of the first holder and benefits go to the first holder's account.
hints: Records are in the first holder's name.

questions.q: Under the SEBI dispute resolution framework applicable to PMS, which ODR stages are free of cost for investors?
questions.explanation: Section 8.6: 'The first two stages are free of cost for the investors.'
hints: Arbitration is not included as free in the workbook.
Only the first two are stated as free.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four purposes of an Investment Policy Statement listed in the workbook?
options: Helping investors form realistic return expectations
Providing a framework for evaluating the portfolio manager
Protecting the investor against inappropriate or unethical decisions
Guaranteeing a minimum return to the investor
questions.explanation: Section 9.3.2: realistic expectations, effective decisions, an evaluation framework and protection from inappropriate/unethical behaviour.
hints: Correct: an IPS never guarantees returns.

questions.q: Section 9A of the Income-tax Act requires an eligible investment fund to have a minimum of how many members who are not connected persons?
questions.explanation: Section 10.3, condition (e): a minimum of 25 members who are, directly or indirectly, not connected persons.

questions.q: A portfolio manager can invest up to what percentage of a client's AUM in the equity of a SINGLE associate or related party?
questions.explanation: Section 11.4 table: single associate 15% (equity, or debt/hybrid), multiple associates 25%, total 30%.
hints: 30% is the overall cap across equity, debt and hybrid.

questions.q: Periodic reports from the portfolio manager to the client must be furnished as agreed but at intervals NOT exceeding:
questions.explanation: Section 11.4: report to the client as agreed in the contract, but not exceeding a period of 3 months.
hints: Allowed, but the maximum interval is 3 months.

questions.q: Which is a common criticism of a market-value weighted index?
options: Large companies have a disproportionate influence on the index
It must be adjusted every time a stock splits
It cannot be used for index funds
questions.explanation: Section 12.3.2: a % change in a large company has greater impact; critics also note overweighting of overvalued stocks.
hints: Value-weighted indices adjust automatically for splits.
They are ideal for index funds.

questions.q: Which form of the efficient market hypothesis says prices reflect all public AND private (insider) information?
questions.explanation: Section 13.2.3: the strong form includes insider information.

questions.q: An investor refuses to sell inherited shares even though they do not fit her strategy, believing they are worth more than the market thinks. This reflects:
questions.explanation: Section 14.3.1: endowment bias; inherited stocks are rarely sold even if they do not fit the strategy.
hints: Framing is about how a question is presented.
Anchoring relies on an initial number.
Correct: valuing what one owns more highly.
Satisficing under limits, not overvaluing ownership.

questions.q: A portfolio manager must buy 1 million shares quoted at a bid of ₹99 and ask of ₹101. Using the workbook's proportional bid-ask measure, the liquidity cost is:
questions.explanation: Section 17.4.4 example: proportional spread = 2/100 = 0.02; liquidity cost = ₹100 mn x 0.02 = ₹2 mn.
hints: Half the spread, not the workbook method.

questions.q: Smart beta strategies are best described as:
options: Rule-based index construction using factors chosen by the manager, lying between passive and active management
Full replication of a market-cap index
questions.explanation: Section 18.5: smart beta uses rule-based selection (like passive) with factors designed by the manager (like active).

questions.q: A manager who believes the market will fall wants to hedge a diversified equity portfolio. The simplest derivative action is to:
options: Sell put options on the index
Buy call options on the index
questions.explanation: Section 18.12: to protect against a fall, she can sell index futures; the futures gain offsets the portfolio loss.
hints: Correct: gains on short futures offset portfolio losses.
Adds upside exposure, not a hedge.

questions.q: Which risk is NOT significant when investing in Government of India securities?
questions.explanation: Chapter 19 sample question and Section 4: government securities carry practically no default risk.
hints: Present: coupons reinvested at uncertain rates.
Correct: G-secs carry practically no default risk.

questions.q: A floating rate bond with 8 years to maturity resets its coupon every quarter. Its duration at any point is at most about:
options: The time remaining until the next coupon reset
Equal to that of an 8-year zero-coupon bond
questions.explanation: Section 19.3.1: maximum duration of a floater is only the remaining time to the next reset, even if maturity is longer.
hints: Floaters are not sensitive like fixed bonds over full maturity.

questions.q: Which measure divides a portfolio's excess return over the risk-free rate by its beta?
questions.explanation: Section 20.4.2: Treynor = (Rp - Rf)/βp.
hints: Uses tracking error and benchmark return.

questions.q: What is the expected return of the client's portfolio?
questions.explanation: Portfolio expected return = Σ wᵢE(Rᵢ) = 8.4 + 4.0 = 12.4% (Section 15.6).
hints: Arithmetic slip: it would need Stock B to return 11%.
questions.case: A portfolio manager holds two stocks for a client: 60% in Stock A and 40% in Stock B. Analysts expect Stock A to return 14% and Stock B 10% next year. Stock A's beta is 1.3 and Stock B's beta is 0.8. The risk-free rate is 6% and the market risk premium is 7%. Assume markets are in CAPM equilibrium for judging valuation.

questions.q: What is the portfolio's beta?
questions.explanation: Portfolio beta is the weighted average of individual betas (Section 20.3.3).

Stock A's beta is 1.3 and Stock B's beta is 0.8. The risk-free rate is 6% and the market risk premium is 7%. Assume markets are in CAPM equilibrium for judging valuation.

questions.q: Comparing the portfolio's expected return with its CAPM required return, the portfolio:
options: Plots above the SML and appears undervalued
Plots below the SML and appears overvalued (required 13.7% vs expected 12.4%)
Cannot be judged without the standard deviation
questions.explanation: CAPM required = 6% + 1.10 x 7% = 13.7%. Expected 12.4% < 13.7%, so it plots below the SML: overvalued (Section 16.9).
hints: Expected is lower than required, so it is below the SML.
SML judgement uses beta, not SD.
